description: Plcsense enables AI agents to understand your TwinCAT libraries and docs, so they write against the real API, not memory.
notes: - docs: issue reports may carry project details, hence off by default
The coding agent writes each report and plcsense cannot control what it
puts in it. The installer checkbox, the terminal question, the privacy
notice, the CLI help, README, SPEC and the IT admin page now say so
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>, [71b61d9](https://github.com/Zeugwerk/plcsense/commit/71b61d91e447aa3f16485fac826fb3c907dd0b07)
- feat: plcsense mcp reads the issue-report choice from the install
report_plcsense_feedback is now on when the install marker says
"feedback": true (installer checkbox, plcsense install --feedback on),
or with --enable-feedback as before. Install and setup no longer write
the flag for an install with a marker, so unticking issue reports takes
effect for every app without rewriting their configs. The flag stays for
setup --feedback, older entries, per-project opt-in and copies without
a marker. AGENTS.md rule 7 and the specs say so
In a terminal, plcsense install now asks the installer's options
(automatic updates on Windows, usage statistics, issue reports) unless
given as options, and lists every app with the found ones ticked instead
of one yes/no for all
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>, [c295ab9](https://github.com/Zeugwerk/plcsense/commit/c295ab9b949251d38ced9be42d4830f8db8e7b43)
- feat: install choices for usage statistics and issue reports
plcsense install --telemetry on|off and --feedback on|off keep the
choice in plcsense.install.json, like --auto-update; a re-run without
them keeps it. Usage statistics are off when the install says so, with
PLCSENSE_TELEMETRY=0, "telemetry": false in the user settings, or the
HKLM DisableTelemetry policy. An install that opted in to issue reports
connects its apps with --enable-feedback, and a later plcsense setup
keeps it
The privacy notice now says what the statistics carry (licence ID, no
project data) and how to turn either off

- feat: improve iss wording, [a238a3e](https://github.com/Zeugwerk/plcsense/commit/a238a3e9975960d94c96a084b8edab1b1cb24775)
- fix: post-update step no longer takes over another install's apps
Starting any copy of a new version ran the post-update step, which used
plcsense install's takeover rule: an installer or script copy repointed
every agent entry that named another working plcsense to itself. A
second downloaded copy started once was enough to pull Cursor and Claude
away from the installed one. Taking over is now only for an explicit
plcsense install; the post-update step only repairs entries whose binary
is gone (and a Scoop copy moves versioned paths to current)

- feat(installer): install.sh becomes a small bootstrapper
curl -fsSL https://plcsense.com/install.sh | bash now asks /version
(tool=plcsense, the only tool the API has a version for), downloads the
platform build by explicit version with the bearer token (HTTP 200 and
gzip checks, PLCSENSE_DOWNLOAD_URL override kept), extracts it into a
staging folder inside <prefix>/share/plcsense, sets the executable bit,
checks that the build knows plcsense install, renames the payload over
the old files (works while plcsense runs) and hands over to
plcsense install --record-channel script --add-to-path --bin-dir
<prefix>/bin, with stdin from /dev/tty when there is one
The .NET check, the privacy text, licence handling, agent detection, the
evaluation request and the profile editing are gone: plcsense does them
bash 3.2 safe, everything in functions, main "$@" on the last line
shellcheck clean. A test keeps the default token the same in the MSBuild
property, install.ps1 and install.sh
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>, [3a7334d](https://github.com/Zeugwerk/plcsense/commit/3a7334dacc3c03d7cb60c439b5b9f68fcd65e42f)
- feat(installer): install.ps1 becomes a small bootstrapper
irm https://plcsense.com/install.ps1 | iex now downloads the current
self-contained build (/version, then /download with the bearer token),
checks the gzip header, extracts it with Windows' tar.exe into a staging
folder inside %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\plcsense (PLCSENSE_INSTALL_DIR),
checks Authenticode (Valid, O=Zeugwerk GmbH) on the exe, checks that the
build knows plcsense install, checks the DLL signatures, swaps the files
in (running files are renamed aside, rollback on failure) and hands over
to plcsense install --record-channel script --add-to-path
ASCII only, Windows PowerShell 5.1 and Constrained Language Mode safe:
cmdlets and tar.exe only, no Add-Type, no New-Object, no static .NET
calls except the guarded TLS 1.2 line, no exit (everything runs in one
script block), no Scoop, no execution policy change. The default token
is a constant at the top (PLCSENSE_TOKEN overrides it)
Tested in Constrained Language Mode against the live API: it stops with
a clear message while the API still serves a build without install

- feat(installer): thin Inno wrapper around plcsense install
The installer now embeds the self-contained plcsense.exe and its two
tree-sitter DLLs ({#PayloadDir}, default ..\publish), installs them per
user to {autopf}\plcsense (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\plcsense) and runs
plcsense install --record-channel installer --add-to-path. No Scoop, no
PowerShell, no download, no token handling

running files to *.old-<timestamp>.*; CloseApplications=no. The
"plcsense is running" checks are gone

skipped when an installed plcsense (own copy or a Scoop copy) passes
license status. Agent detection, licence parsing and the notify call
moved into plcsense
- Silent switches and their env fallbacks stay (/ACCEPTPRIVACY /EMAIL
/LICENSEKEY /CREATOR /AGENTS /ZKMAKE); key and email reach plcsense

- Progress from --progress-file, the finish page from --result-file
(apps, licence, evaluation note, Scoop copy note). Setup exit code
0 / 1 / 2 through GetCustomSetupExitCode
- Uninstallable: unins000.exe runs plcsense uninstall first. The

- feat(cli): install, update, uninstall and license evaluate
All install logic now lives in the plcsense binary, on top of
Zeugwerk.Installation:
- plcsense install: privacy notice, licence (already / key / Creator /
evaluation request), app detection and MCP configs, zkmake skill
(never installs zkmake), repair of stale config paths, PATH (HKCU PATH
first on Windows; symlink plus marked profile block on Linux/macOS),
install marker, progress and result files for the Inno wizard, install
log with secrets masked. Exit 0 / 1 / 2 (key not activated)
- plcsense update [--check] [--allow-unsigned]: manual update for
installer and script installs; refuses Scoop and dev copies with the
next step. --check exits 0 / 10 / 1
- plcsense uninstall: removes this install's MCP entries and PATH
changes; deletes the folder on Linux/macOS, prints it on Windows
- plcsense license evaluate --email: the /notify evaluation request,
skipped on a licensed machine
- MCP server start: background cleanup, post-update step (repoints agent
configs on the first start of a new version) and, on Windows, the
automatic updater after about a minute. Nothing goes to stdout
- setup writes the canonical path (installer/script binary, Scoop
current, or the running binary), refuses temp locations without
--force, and remembers the connected app
- Agent detection moved from the installer and both scripts into
AgentDetector. McpSetupService can read, repoint and remove the
plcsense entry. The privacy notice lists the evaluation request and
updates with their opt-outs (also in installer/privacy.txt)
license status, license activate and setup's zkmake flags keep their
output and exit codes for installers and scripts already in the field

- feat: reusable install and update component (Zeugwerk.Installation)
Adds src/Zeugwerk.Installation, a product-neutral project that holds the
generic install and self-update logic, and its own test project:
- download API client (/version, /download) with the bearer token sent
only to the API host, also after redirects; system proxy with default
credentials on Windows
- version parsing like Scoop's checkver regex, comparison on the API's
components, never a downgrade
- tar.gz extraction of named root files, gzip check, executable bit
- Authenticode verification through WinVerifyTrust plus the signer O=
- install marker, channel detection, Scoop copy detection (old and new
Scoop file names), transient locations
- update eligibility per channel and platform, user opt-out, IT policy
- update lock (named mutex / lock file), apply sequence with swap and
rollback, startup cleanup, Apps & Features DisplayVersion
- automatic-update scheduler (24 h gate, backoff), post-update trigger
- PATH handling: HKCU PATH prepend (keeps REG_EXPAND_SZ), POSIX symlink
and marked profile block
- install log with secret masking, progress file, result file
- evaluation request (/notify)
A test fails if the component's sources name a product
